Hi Michael / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- You are evaluating Redwood to power clinical summarization and patient messaging use cases.
- You confirmed those features will process PHI (patient identifiers, encounter metadata, free-text notes) at least in the short term.
- Security is the blocker for procurement: SOC 2 status, BAA availability, and answers to the vendor security questionnaire.

What we can do / immediate next steps:
1) BAA eligibility: Redwood can sign a BAA for customers using Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). Hosted shared-tier API is not eligible for PHI/BAA scenarios without a Private deployment. See attached "Redwood_prelim_BAA_summary.docx" for a short checklist.

2) PHI handling boundaries: short answers below — will follow up with Neha (our security lead) on details:
   - Data in requests for PHI-sensitive workloads should go to Dedicated or Private only.
   - KV/prefix caching is disabled for PHI workloads by default under BAA terms.
   - Persistent logs containing content are restricted; audit logs and token-level usage can be provided with retention limits.

3) SOC 2: Redwood currently maintains SOC 2 Type II (we can provide the report under NDA).

4) Vendor questionnaire: thanks for sending your questionnaire during the call — I attached MedHealth_vendor_questionnaire.pdf back to this thread and asked Neha to start filling the security answers.

Action items:
- Michael / Sara: confirm whether you need Dedicated or Private (if you need VPC connectivity or on-prem air-gapped options, we should treat this as Private).
- Michael: confirm timeline for procurement and whether you want the SOC 2 report now (NDA) or during contract review.
- Neha: can you take the questionnaire and add RFC answers / gaps?
- Dylan: I'll loop you for any technical clarifications about network connectivity and model pinning.

If it helps, I can put together a short one-pager that maps "Redwood deployment mode" -> "BAA eligible / PHI allowed" and highlight operational controls (cache, logs, KMS).

Thanks — talk soon.

Hi Michael —

Short answers up front: 
- Hosted/shared API: not BAA-eligible for PHI at this time. We do not offer BAAs for shared multitenant endpoints.
- Dedicated + Private: both are BAA-eligible. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity in our cloud with data isolation; Private gives you VPC or on-prem options with customer-managed networking and optional air-gapped deployments.

More detail / controls (high level):
- Caching: KV/prefix caching is disabled for PHI under BAA. Transient inference caches are not persisted to customer-visible storage.
- Logs & Metrics: we can provide audit logs and token-level cost telemetry with configurable retention; content redaction policies can be applied.
- Key management: KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated; HSM options available for Private deployments.
- Model pinning & rollouts: you can pin a model binary for consistent behavior across rollouts; fallback to a non-BAA model is possible but would not be allowed to process PHI.

Attached: Redwood_security_answers.xlsx (initial pass), and I asked Neha to review and expand where we need formal language for procurement/legal.

Neha — can you add the SOC 2 doc note and the specific BAA language (standard indemnities, data processing scope) in the spreadsheet? If you want, I can coordinate a 30-min call between your team and Michael/Sara next week.

Michael — if you confirm Dedicated vs Private preference, Dylan and I will scope network work and provide a short tech checklist for procurement.

Best,
Marissa
